AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
 verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
 glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
 using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings are also
 archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk's Office.
 If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 Library, Arts and Culture Department, at (818) 548-2030, during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  SEPTEMBER 16, 2021 AT 2:00 PM

To help slow the transmission of COVID-19, and protect the health and safety of the community, City
Council, as well as Board & Commission meetings, will continue to be closed to the public for in-person
attendance.
The public is encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social
distancing. Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and
AT&T U-verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire devices
using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu.
For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a
specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed.
 1. REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA – 2:00 PM
  Roll Call
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the September 16, 2021
  Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission was Posted on
  September 9, 2021 on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.
2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the July 15, 2021 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission

  b. Minutes of the August 31, 2021 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission

3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Principal

  Arts & Culture Administrator

4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
5. ACTION ITEMS
  a. “Be the Change” Series

  1. Motion approving the funding of the “Be the Change” Series in an amount not to
  exceed $40,000 from the 2021- 2022 Work Plan.
  b. Storefront Art Program

  1. Motion approving the funding of a pilot Storefront Art Program in an amount not to
  exceed $25,000 from the 2021- 2022 Work Plan.
  c. Nomination of one Commissioner for the Artist Review & Selection Committee for
  the City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ

  1. Motion appointing one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for
  the City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ.
6. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS
  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update
  ii. Beyond the Box – Update
  iii. LeBasse Projects – RFQ Update
  iv. Mural Ordinance – Update
   2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update
  3. PERFORMING ARTS
  i. Brand Library Plaza Series - Update
  ii. 222 East Concert Series – Update
  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update

  b. Marketing and Communications for Arts and Culture projects in Glendale
  1. Marketing and Communications Assessment of Arts and Culture
  Commission Programs

7. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS
9. ADJOURNMENT
  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is Thursday,
  October 21, 2021, at 2:00 PM via teleconference only.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, September 16, 2021 at 2:00 p.m.
1.  ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on September 16, 2021 at 2:09 p.m.
  •  Present: Commissioner Viar, Vidor, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  •  Absent: Commissioner Zadorian
  •  The Agenda for the September 16, 2021 Regular Meeting was posted on September 9, 2021 on the
  Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2.  CONSENT ITEMS (INCLUDING MINUTES)
  a.  Minutes of the July 15, 2021 Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission (Approved as
  Amended)
  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Zadorian, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  b. Minutes of the August 31, 2021 Special Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission

  Moved:  Commissioner Viar
  Seconded: Vice Chair Yank

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

3.  INTRODUCTIONS & PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Jennifer Fukutomi-Jones, Arts and Culture Commission
  Administrator.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave an overview of current and upcoming events at Glendale Library, Arts
  & Culture locations.

4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Speaker(s): None

  1
 5. ACTION ITEMS

  a. “Be the Change” Series

  1. Motion approving the funding of the “Be the Change” Series in an amount not to exceed $40,000
  from the 2021- 2022 Work Plan.
  •  Nicole Pasini, Assistant Director of Glendale Library, and Tiffany Barrios, Senior Glendale
  Library Supervisor, gave a brief summary and update of the “Be the Change” Series. The
  Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves funding of the “Be the Change” Series in
  an amount not to exceed $40,000 from the 2021-2022 Work Plan, as more fully outlined in the
  September 16, 2021 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  b. Storefront Art Program

  1. Motion approving the funding of a pilot Storefront Art Program in an amount not to exceed $25,000
  from the 2021- 2022 Work Plan.
  •  Loreto Lopez, former 2020 Claremont Graduate University Arts Management Student
  Consultant, gave the Commission a detailed presentation and her recommendations
  regarding the upcoming pilot Storefront Art program. The Commission asked questions and
  gave their feedback.

  Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby approves funding of a pilot Storefront Art Program in
  an amount not to exceed $25,000 from the 2021-2022 Work Plan, the costs of which must be
  rebalanced between art reception, artists’ stipend, and production, as more fully outlined in the
  September 16, 2021 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

  c. Nomination of one Commissioner for the Artist Review & Selection Committee for the City-Wide
  Public Art Landmarks RFQ

  1. Motion appointing one Commissioner to the Artist Review & Selection Committee for the City-Wide
  Public Art Landmarks RFQ.
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a summary of the nomination process and answered questions by
  the Commission. The Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  2
   Moved:  Commissioner Vidor
  Seconded: Commissioner Viar

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby appoints Commissioner / Vice Chair Yank to the
  Artist Review & Selection Committee for the City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ, as more fully
  outlined in the September 16, 2021 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator.

  Ayes:  Commissioners Viar, Vidor, Vice Chair Yank, Chairperson Tufenkian
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian
  Abstain:  None

6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2021-2022 Work Plan Progress Updates
  1. CITY-WIDE ARTS

  i. Art Happens Anywhere – Projects Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a brief update on the ongoing and upcoming AHA projects,
  including: Verdugo Skate Park Mural, Meter Pole Art Project, Public Art piece “Lightwaves,”
  and temporary public art exhibit “Impending Storms.” She also stated 10 out of 17 Art
  Happens Anywhere projects have been successfully launched. Two projects are in the
  process of being launched, and 5 projects are in the process of determining final logistics.

  ii. Beyond the Box – Update

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones gave a brief update and stated that on August 31, 2021, Staff met with the
  Artist Review & Selection Committee for the Beyond the Box – Utility Box Mural Art Program.
  The theme of this year’s program is “Celebrating Mental Health Awareness.” Staff received 60
  applications for consideration, and the Artist Review & Selection Committee chose 8 finalists
  for this year’s program. Painting of the utility boxes will take place from October 22-24, 2021.

  iii. LeBasse Projects – RFQ Update

  •  LeBasse Projects released the City-Wide Public Art Landmarks RFQ on August 16, 2021, and
  has been reaching out to various networks of artists to share about this opportunity. The
  application deadline has been extended and will close on October 8, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.
  iv. Mural Ordinance – Update
  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that Ms. Odenkirk will be drafting recommendations on policies
  and procedures for artists’ submitting and the City’s processing murals on private property
  and City property, in addition to criteria for the Commission’s evaluating and approving the
  murals. Staff will provide an update on the mural approval processes and procedures at the
  Commission’s October 16, 2021 Regular Meeting.

  2. NEIGHBORHOOD ARTS – No Update

  3
   3. PERFORMING ARTS
  i. Brand Library Plaza Series – Update

  The Brand Library Plaza Series kicked-off on August 13, 2021, featuring Black Market Reverie.
  There are 2 remaining concert dates for the series:
  Friday, September 17, 2021 at 7:00 pm: The ROAMies
  Friday, September 24, 2021 at 7:00 pm: Reckless Night Ensemble
  For more information, please visit: https://www.glendaleartsandculture.org/brandplazaseries

  ii. 222 East Concert Series – Update
  Staff has confirmed the following dates and artists for the 2021 222 East Concert Series which will
  be located at the Artsakh Paseo between Broadway and Wilson St.:
  Saturday, October 2, 2021 at 4:00 pm: Paris Chansons
  Saturday, October 9, 2021 at 4:00 pm: MoForro
  Saturday, October 16, 2021 at 4:00 pm: Kotolan
  Saturday, October 23, 2021 at 4:00 pm: Coveted Future
  Saturday, October 30, 2021 at 4:00 pm: Igor Kogan Quintet
  For more information, please visit: https://www.glendaleartsandculture.org/222east

  4. ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS – No Update
  b. Marketing and Communications for Arts and Culture projects in Glendale
  1. Marketing and Communications Assessment of Arts and Culture Commission
  Programs

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones introduced 2021 Claremont Graduate University Arts Management
  Student Consultant, Yasmin Bouhafs. Ms. Bouhafs presented her findings and
  recommendations for enhancing marketing and communication efforts. The Commission
  asked questions and gave their feedback.

6. COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS
  • Commissioner Vidor stated she enjoyed the Brand Plaza Series and thanked everyone
  involved. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones thanked Brand Library staff and Glendale Youth Alliance for
  their work with the Brand Plaza Series.

8. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

9. ADJOURNMENT – 3:53 pm

The next Regular Meeting of the Arts and Culture Commission is October 21, 2021, at 2:00 p.m., in City
Council Chambers (2nd Floor), 613 E. Broadway.
